cover.headline: The strongest long-run record of the four small-cap funds compared — deepest history, one manager across the whole of it, every 5-year window positive — set against a real, category-wide correction it is sitting inside right now. Own it for the base rate, not the last twelve months.

coverage.lede: A fund is judged on two pillars, not on last year's number: the record it has actually delivered across full cycles, and the quality of the book it holds now. This deck keeps the two separate — and keeps 'is this fund good' apart from 'is this category worth adding to today'.

identity.title: A pure small-cap book, run by one hand since day one
identity.lede: The deepest history of the four funds compared — 7.75 years live, spanning the 2020 crash, the 2022 correction and the 2025 small-cap de-rating — every year of it credited to the same manager.
identity.footer: Sources · AMFI 145206 · Tickertape fund id · IndMoney fund_id 1002043

cells: Tata Asset Management — Tata-group-backed, no SEBI/governance flags
GARP — growth at a reasonable price

glance.title: Six reads, weighed separately
glance.lede: Each pillar carries its own stance and its own confidence. The record is strong and well-evidenced; the near-term and the look-through are where the caution sits.
glance.footer: Stance is this run's read of each dimension — not a rating agency's.

lenses.name: The record
lenses.read: Every 5Y rolling window ≥ +15%, 98% of them beating the benchmark. Deepest, most consistent of the four.

lenses.name: Near-term
lenses.read: Trails the category average on all six measured windows; 1Y +0.65% vs category +14.55%. Real, not noise.

lenses.name: Look-through
lenses.read: Priced slice covers only ~20% of AUM on a stale book — can't confirm the current portfolio is cheap.

lenses.name: Cap purity
lenses.read: 84.8% small / 8.1% mid / 0% large — the truest-to-label small-cap mandate of the four.

lenses.name: Cost
lenses.read: 0.40% Direct TER, cost-rank 1 in category. Nothing to argue with here.

lenses.name: AMC & manager
lenses.read: Clean pedigree, 7.75y single-manager tenure, and a rare valuation-driven capital-discipline signal.

perf.title: Every five-year holder has made at least 15% a year
perf.lede: Rolling returns — every possible holding window, not one lucky endpoint — are the metric that matters. On the long windows Tata's record is the best of the four funds; on the short ones it is mid-correction.
perf.footer: NAV-derived · benchmark = Nifty Smallcap 250 index-fund proxy · 1,911 daily obs
perf.workings_label: How the rolling record is computed
perf.workings: Daily-rolled windows over the full NAV series: for each window length the mean, median and minimum across every start date, with the count of windows (n). A positive minimum 5Y return means no five-year holder in the fund's life has lost money. Sharpe 0.90 at 6% risk-free; point-to-point CAGR is kept only for reference (1Y 0.65% · 3Y 13.38% · 5Y 15.49%) because its endpoints decide it.

bars.title: % of rolling windows beating the benchmark

peer.title: Against its peers, the last year is a genuine shortfall
peer.lede: A data cross-check struck the two supports the first read leaned on. Corrected, Tata trails the category average on every single window — the near-term weakness is peer-relative, not a category-wide de-rating.
peer.footer: IndMoney peer data, 14-Aug-2026 · trailing windows, not calendar years
peer.corrections: Two supports removed: (1) the "3/15 on 3Y" rank came from a broken IndMoney field that also reports Tata worst-in-category while beating the worst fund — unusable. (2) The "category-wide −5.5%" defence of the weak 1Y used the CY2025 calendar year, not the trailing 1Y; over the trailing year the category made +14.55% and Tata +0.65%. The near-term shortfall is real and stands.

read.label: The read
read.text: Tata's 3Y (13.39%) sits just above the category's worst fund (13.07%). IndMoney's composite rank of 23/23, tagged "Bad", is directionally consistent — a composite dominated by the current drawdown, not a verdict on long-run skill.

lookthrough.title: The book it holds now, we cannot yet price
lookthrough.lede: Coverage is a gate, not a footnote: ratios computed on a fifth of the fund describe a different fund. The look-through here is directional context, never the valuation verdict.
lookthrough.footer: Look-through compute over cached Nov-2025 holdings weights · coverage gates every ratio

gate.label: COVERAGE ~20% OF AUM
gate.text: 20 disclosed names sum to ~26.6% of the 93.2% equity book; 4 failed to resolve (renames/symbol mismatches). The priced slice skews to recent listings and capital-heavy names, so the portfolio P/E of ~46 is computed on holdings the fund may no longer hold — directional only, not used as the verdict.

distress.label: EARNINGS-DISTRESS DISPERSION
distress.text: 36.6% of the book earns sub-8% ROE — the most depressed of the four funds. ~20% sits in steel/industrial machinery where a policy-backed capex upcycle is demonstrably beginning; ~12.9% in chemicals where the trough is passing but recovery is capped by Chinese overcapacity. But a meaningful slice is idiosyncratic, not cyclical — IDFC First Bank (3.8% ROE) and Wockhardt (4.3%) sit in sectors that are not in downcycles and may not mean-revert.

lookthrough.caution: Low ROE is not automatically a cycle trough. This fund is a leveraged bet on the Indian industrial capex cycle — not a cheap-and-safe holding.

style.title: The truest-to-label small-cap of the four
style.lede: A corrected cap-tilt withdrew a false '19% large-cap drift': this is a pure small-cap mandate with no large-cap exposure at all, holding 62 names — real diversified stock-picking, not closet-indexing and not a concentrated bet.
style.footer: Cap-tilt by SEBI market-cap rank (AMC-disclosed), never ₹Cr bands · drift vs 4-Jul-2026 read

trust.title: A rare, genuine capital-discipline signal
trust.lede: The cleanest manager-attribution story of the four — one manager across the fund's entire record — and an AMC that closed the fund to lump-sums on its own valuation conviction, not to gather assets.
trust.footer: Sources · angelone.in reopening notice · valueresearchonline.com Padiyar interview · equitymaster.com Nov-2025 note

checks.label: AMC pedigree — Tata AM, no red flags
Manager tenure covers the whole record
Closed to lump-sums when valuations rich

discipline.label: WHY THIS MATTERS
discipline.text: The fund stopped taking lump-sum money for nearly three years — SIP/STP only — explicitly because small-cap valuations were elevated, and reopened in April 2026 with the AMC's stated reason being that valuations had moderated after the 2025 correction. A valuation-driven reopening, not asset-gathering: investor-first capital discipline that also reads as consistency with the stated GARP process.

cost.title: Cheap fund, and the category is no longer expensive
cost.lede: Two different questions, answered separately. The fund itself is among the cheapest in its category; the category has already been through the correction that makes an entry more defensible than it was a year ago.
cost.footer: Cost from IndMoney cost-rank · category valuation stance from get_market_context

band.note: The AMC reopened the fund on its own read that small-cap valuations had moderated after the 2025 de-rating. 'Is this fund good' and 'is this the moment to add small-cap' are different calls — the fund is a hold on quality; the entry is more defensible than a year ago but the near-term drawdown is not over.

verdict.title: Hold it for the base rate, watch the book
verdict.lede: The strongest past-performance case of the four, offset by a real mid-correction near-term and a look-through too thin to confirm the current book is cheap rather than merely beaten down. The recommendation is a hold with a non-price review trigger.
verdict.footer: The switch decision belongs to portfolio-review — it alone sees exit loads, tax and the whole book

conditions.why: Would turn a defensible entry into an attractive one.

conditions.condition: Look-through coverage improves and shows the book expensive
conditions.why: The one thing the record cannot rule out today.

conditions.condition: Style drift — large-cap creep or index-hugging
conditions.why: The purity and the stock-picking are half the case.

verdict.review: Review if the manager changes, if small-cap P/B falls below its median, or if a fuller look-through shows the book expensive — never on a price move alone.

position.label: If you hold it
position.text: Keep it for the base rate; do not add on the weak 1Y alone. If you are choosing fresh money in small-cap today, this is a defensible pick on quality and cost — but hand the switch/rebalance decision to portfolio-review, which sees your whole book.

verdict.plan_note: A shortlist is the input to a verdict, not the verdict. This is one named call with numbered triggers.

gaps.title: What this review does not know
gaps.lede: Every gap is labelled, never papered over. A partial-book ratio is withheld, not caveated — it describes a different fund.

items.label: LOOK-THROUGH COVERAGE
items.text: P/E, P/B and ROE are computed on only ~20% of AUM — 4 of 20 disclosed holdings failed to price. Treated as directional context, never the valuation verdict.

items.label: STALE HOLDINGS
items.text: The disclosed book is a Nov-2025 snapshot; the 7-Aug-2026 top holding is Kirloskar Pneumatic at 6.55%, more concentrated than reported. The priced P/E is on names the fund may no longer hold.

items.label: BENCHMARK PROXY
items.text: Rolling-return win-rate uses a Nifty Smallcap 250 index-fund proxy, not the raw TR index.

items.label: PORTFOLIO DEPTH
items.text: Only the top-20 of 62 holdings are obtainable via IndMoney; the long tail is unpriced.

gaps.weakest: The weakest link is coverage: the record is strong and well-attributed, but the case for the price of the current book rests on ~20% of it. A fuller look-through is the single thing that would most move this verdict.
